title: PolyServe: Efficient Multi-SLO Serving at Scale
technique: bins requests by per-token latency (TPOT) tier into server clusters, routes to highest-load still-SLO-attainable server, per-tier autoscaling, wait-time-aware scheduling and dynamic chunking

optimized_metrics.evidence: we propose PolyServe, a novel multi-SLO scheduling policy at scale that maintains high SLO attainment while maximizing throughput.
maintains high SLO attainment while maximizing throughput
a good policy must use as few servers as possible while attaining the SLO.
the i-th token must be produced before TTFT + i * TPOT ... Due to this flexibility, we adopt DSLO in this paper.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: the i-th token must be produced before TTFT + i * TPOT

headline_claim.text: PolyServe achieves 1.23x goodput gain compared to existing policies, achieving up to 92.5% of optimal goodput.

reported_metrics.where: overall and per-TPOT-tier breakdown, load sweep figure
goodput at 90% attainment; Fig 9 per-instance goodput
Fig 8 cost per request (instance x seconds)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Time to First Token (TTFT), measured from request submission to the generation of the first token
Time per Output Token (TPOT), measuring the time between consecutive tokens.
metric_definitions.notes: TPOT defined as inter-token time but enforced via deadline: 'the i-th token must be produced before TTFT + i · TPOT'; paper notes 'some works target average TPOT' vs 'adhering to maximum TPOT can be too restrictive'

metric_definitions.definition_quote: a deadline-based SLO (DSLO) [22]. Specifically, the i-th token must be produced before TTFT + i · TPOT.
metric_definitions.notes: cumulative per-token deadline, lets provider delay early tokens

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We define the cost as instance · second, meaning the total time spent on the instance for serving this request. For example, with a batch size B that is served on an instance of N GPUs, taking T to finish, the total cost is NT, and thus the per-request cost is NT/B.
At 90% attainment, PD-PolyServe and CO-PolyServe provide on average 1.23x and 1.18x more goodput than the best baseline.
metric_definitions.notes: no standalone formal definition; operationally request rate at which overall SLO attainment is 90%

slo_spec: Fixed (TTFT, TPOT) tiers. Eval: TTFT sampled uniformly from 300/500/1000 ms; TPOT tiers 20/30/50/100 ms with probability 10/20/30/40%; SLO assigned only if achievable on an idle server; goodput at 90% attainment; example provider tiers (1000ms,20ms),(1000ms,30ms),(2000ms,50ms), best-effort
load_regime: request-rate sweep (20%-120% of optimal throughput), Poisson; burstiness test with inverted tier mix
tradeoff_acknowledged: tighter SLO restricts batching, lowering utilization and raising cost; chunked prefill adds extra iterations (tail TTFT)
hardware: profiling traces from NVIDIA H200; 20 simulated instances
workloads: mooncake, lmsys, sharegpt, splitwise traces (300k sampled requests), synthetic uniform lengths; SLOs synthetic
